flawed_step: The universal step 'triangle-free with Delta<=4 implies a proper 3-coloring exists' cannot be justified: the Chvatal graph is a triangle-free 4-regular graph with chromatic number 4.
counterexample: Chvatal graph on vertices 0..11 with edges 0-1,0-4,0-6,0-9,1-2,1-5,1-7,2-3,2-6,2-8,3-4,3-7,3-9,4-5,4-8,5-10,5-11,6-10,6-11,7-8,7-11,8-10,9-10,9-11. It is 4-regular (N(0)={1,4,6,9}, N(1)={0,2,5,7}, N(2)={1,3,6,8}, N(3)={2,4,7,9}, N(4)={0,3,5,8}, N(5)={1,4,10,11}, N(6)={0,2,10,11}, N(7)={1,3,8,11}, N(8)={2,4,7,10}, N(9)={0,3,10,11}, N(10)={5,6,8,9}, N(11)={5,6,7,9}). It is triangle-free: for each of the 24 edges, the endpoints have no common neighbour. It is not 3-colorable. If c(10)!=c(11), say 1 and 2, then 5, 6 and 9 must be 3; every vertex of the 5-cycle 0-1-2-3-4 is adjacent to one of 5, 6, 9, so the odd cycle would be 2-colored, which is impossible. If c(10)=c(11)=1, then 5..9 use {2,3}; the only edge among them is 7-8, so WLOG 7=2 and 8=3. This forces c1,c3 in {1,3} and c2,c4 in {1,2}, and the pairs (c1,c4), (c0,c2), (c0,c3) must not be {2,3} (because of vertices 5, 6, 9). All branches (c1,c2) in {(1,2),(3,1),(3,2)} fail: each forces vertex 6 or vertex 9 to see both 2 and 3.
assessment_summary: False. The Chvatal graph (12 vertices, 4-regular, triangle-free) needs 4 colors. Triangle-freeness and degrees were checked edge by edge, and non-3-colorability was shown by a complete case analysis on whether vertices 10 and 11 share a color.
